content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement back to the disclosure.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. I checked all 22 claims (apparatus claims 1-17, method claims 18-22) limitation by limitation, all 27 reference numerals in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part call-out in all seven figure briefs and in the detailed description, the Summary, Abstract, Brief Description of Drawings, and every material, shape, position, connection, operating condition, and variant, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md (input/conversation.md contains only a truncated copy of the same USER passage and adds nothing; input/request.md is a resume/repair instruction and was treated as non-affirmative). Every technical assertion traced: rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot through the rail, printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge, two screws in two corresponding holes, reversal moving the projecting portion between longitudinal sides while the same marked upper face stays readable; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages each with a lower anti-rotation key in the slot, one cylindrical hardened-metal replaceable drill bushing with a vertical bore passing completely through the carriage and registering with the slot, bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob with a shank through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe and releasing on loosening; a pointer on each carriage aligned with its bore axis and readable against the distance marks, their difference being the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the full method sequence (select spacing, loosen, slide to a difference centered on the index, tighten, place, press fence or spacer plate to the edge, align notch and index to the centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing left attached); rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers and knobs; hardened metal replaceable bushings; and the absence of motor, battery, sensor, and network connection. No untraced structure, material, proportion, count, or relationship was found; the depiction conventions (plain block carriages, plain round knobs, plain rectangular fence, schematic slot and notch) are confined to figure briefs, are expressly schematic, and add no functional geometry, and no "by way of example" or shape-broadening language appears in the application text. Section-line designations are consistent across FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 5 and the Brief Description (3-3 through carriage 70, 5-5 through carriage 50, arrows both toward the fence, matching FIG. 4's stated viewing direction); each numeral has one meaning, every figure numeral list matches its brief text, and no numeral in the ledger is unused; claim and description terminology agree and all brief-mandated terms are preserved; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains; antecedent basis and abstract length (146 words) are in order. Two minor internal-consistency defects remain, both confined to figure briefs and both fixable without adding any unsupported matter: FIG. 7 asks for a single straight centerline that cannot simultaneously align with a mid-length transverse stroke and an end notch, and FIG. 2 depicts the entire rail including its second end while omitting the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 that FIG. 7 places there.

findings.title: FIG. 7 brief requires one straight centerline to be aligned simultaneously with the mid-length transverse center index 24 and with the sight notch 26 at the second end
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, paragraphs describing the transverse center index 24 and the centerline 94
findings.detail: FIG. 7 fixes the transverse center index 24 as a stroke running across the rail at the mid-length position ("in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end") and the sight notch 26 as a notch in the second end at the right of the band, and then asks for one straight pencil line on the workpiece to be aligned with both. A straight line collinear with a transverse stroke at the midpoint runs across the rail, so it cannot also pass through a notch located a substantial distance away at the second end; a renderer must therefore invent one geometry or the other. The specification and claims restate the source faithfully ("a sight notch formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the transverse center index"), so no application text needs changing; only the figure brief over-commits to an undrawable single-line depiction.
findings.evidence: FIG-7.md: "A transverse center index 24 is a single straight stroke of visible thickness lying on the upper surface of the rail 10 in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10. It runs transverse to the length of the rail 10." and "A centerline 94 is a straight pencil line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, with which the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned." Disclosure: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint. A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index." and "slides the carriages until their pointer readings have the desired difference and are centered about the transverse center index" (which requires the index to mark a definite lengthwise position).
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the centerline sentence with: "A centerline 94 is a straight pencil line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, running transverse to the length of the rail 10 in line with the transverse center index 24, visible on the workpiece 90 on both long sides of the rail 10 and hidden where the rail 10 covers it." Leave the sight notch sentence as "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10, shown schematically." and do not require the depicted centerline 94 to pass through the sight notch 26. Make no change to draft/08-detailed-description.md or to claims 5, 6 and 18, which restate the disclosure verbatim.

findings.title: FIG. 2 depicts the entire rail including its second end but omits the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 that FIG. 7 shows formed there
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (body text and "Numerals shown on this figure" list); cf. figures/FIG-7.md
findings.detail: FIG. 2 is a top plan view of the whole jig with the rail "extend[ing] across the drawing area from left to right", i.e. it shows the second end of the rail 10 in the same orientation and view type as FIG. 7. The brief lists only 10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 62, 70, 82, so the rendered second end of the rail will appear plain, contradicting FIG. 7, which shows the shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 formed in that same second end and the transverse center index 24 on the same upper surface. Both features are affirmatively disclosed parts of the rail, so including them in FIG. 2 adds no unsupported matter and removes the discrepancy between the two top plan views before rendering.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "The long, straight rail 10 is seen from above and extends across the drawing area from left to right." with a numeral list containing no 24 or 26. FIG-7.md: "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10" and "A transverse center index 24 ... runs transverse to the length of the rail 10." Disclosure: "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint. A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index."
findings.fix: Add to figures/FIG-2.md, after the distance marks paragraph: "A transverse center index 24 is a short stroke on the upper surface of the rail 10 running transverse to the length of the rail 10 at the midpoint between the two ends. A shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 is formed in the right-hand, second end of the rail 10, shown schematically." and add "- 24: transverse center index" and "- 26: sight notch" to the numeral list of FIG. 2. No change to the numeral ledger or to the application text is required.
